brief: Oil overshot its 200-day moving average and is reversing sharply, in a market the note frames as range-bound. Since oil spiked in August, Democrats' odds of retaking the Senate rose from 41% to above 50%, with Brent near $110/bbl 7.5 weeks before the midterms. Trump said oil stays high until after the midterms then falls sharply, but the administration may feel pressure to ease as the 10-year yield nears 5%, so oil above $100 through the midterms is not certain. DB says oil volatility shows less stress than July's spike or the March shock, suggesting the vol market may already be pricing that reversal. On the yen, faster BoJ tightening, political tolerance for a stronger currency, and reversing capital outflows are now aligning after two years of USD/JPY ignoring collapsing rate differentials. TS Lombard argues repatriation could sustain a break below 150 toward 130-140 fair value, and that rising JPY volatility could force carry-trade deleveraging as intervention turns into a broader unwind. Natixis argues a disorderly yen break could itself trigger a broader volatility event that reset VIX levels could cheaply hedge. A GPIF rotation into JGBs would also cut Japanese demand for foreign debt, pressuring US and European yields.
